notes: Audited the full harvest pipeline for the same privilege-scoping bug fixed for systems in an earlier release. An Active IQ account without unfiltered_system_access must pass watchlistId on EVERY account-scoped query, not just systems -- found riskInstances, cases, customers, sites, sustainabilityScore, systemContractRenewals, and recommendations all still querying unscoped, silently returning empty for any such account. Confirmed live against a real 186-system account: risks 0->298, cases 0->149, recommendations 0->23, sites 0->8, sustainability 0->31 after adding watchlistId scoping to each. While fixing this, found a second bug: a stale top-level legacy watchlistId (left over from before multi-account was configured) was being applied as a blanket filter across every configured account's harvest, so the new risk/case scoping accidentally cross-contaminated a second account's queries with the first account's watchlist ID -- fixed by gating the legacy field to single-account mode only, matching its documented intent. Also fixed the Settings 'resolve watchlist ID' tool, which always authenticated with the wrong account and crashed with an unhelpful error instead of reporting the real cause -- it now tries every configured account and reports which one actually resolved the watchlist.
